newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO PLAY TWICE IN ONE NIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO PLAY TWICE IN ONE NIGHT.

text.p: Brazilian club Cruzeiro played two official matches in one night on Wednesday as they attempted to battle their way through a daunting fixture list.
Cruzeiro faced Vila Nova in the Minas Gerais championship, a Brazilian regional competition, at the Mineirao stadium in Belo Horizonte.
Less than half an hour later, they took the field for their opening match in the Libertadores Cup -- South American's top club competition -- at home to fellow Brazilians Gremio.
Cruzeiro opted to field their reserve team in the first game but consequently had only five substitutes for the main match instead of the permitted seven.
They gleaned at total of only one point from the evening, drawing 4-4 with Vila Nova and then losing 2-1 to Gremio in their first round, group four match in the Libertadores.
Cruzeiro's defeat was not a complete disaster as the Libertadores rules generously stipulate that the top three in each of the four-team first round groups qualify for the second round.
Peruvian sides Sporting Cristal and Alianza, who drew 0-0 in Lima, make up the group and one of them is likeley to finish last.
Gremio, the 1995 Libertadores and 1996 Brazilian champions, played their usual effective game which combines ruthless midfield marking with quick counter-attacks.
Midfielder Emerson scored the winner in the 63rd minute in a game littered with ugly fouls and off-the-ball incidents.
Velez Sarsfield, champions in 1994, also began with an away win in group two as they overcame fellow Argentines Racing Club 2-1 in Buenos Aires.
Patricio Camps scored either side of halftime for Velez with Fernando Queiroz pulling a goal back for Racing with a free kick.

Velez goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, who last year scored nine goals from free kicks and penalties, blasted a free kick against the Racing crossbar in the first half and made a superb double save at the other end to deny Racing.
The other game in the group saw Emelec score five minutes from time to beat fellow Ecuadoreans Nacional 2-1 at home in Guayaquil.
Two teams from each South American country take part but the criteria for which teams enter the tourament varies between nations.
Brazil enters the winners of the national championship -- Gremio -- and the winners of a knockout competition called the Copa Brasil -- Cruzeiro.

Argentina holds two national championships per season and enters the winners of each. Last year, however, Velez won both championships and the second place was taken by Racing, who won a playoff between the runners-up.
Uruguay organises a special mini-league, totally separate from the championship, to find its representatives while Colombia simply sends the winners and runners-up of its national championship.
